QuestionStmt.S: A parallel beam of light is incident normally on a plane surface absorbing 50% of the light and reflecting the rest. If the incident beam carries 90 W of power, the force exerted by it on the surface is ($C = \text{velocity of light in air} = 3 \times 10^8 \, \text{m/s}$)

Solution.S:
Given: Power of incident light $P = 90$ W. Surface absorbs 50% and reflects 50%. Speed of light $c = 3 \times 10^8$ m/s.

Force due to absorption:
$$P_{\text{abs}} = 0.5 \times 90 = 45 \text{ W}$$
$$F_{\text{abs}} = \frac{P_{\text{abs}}}{c} = \frac{45}{3 \times 10^8} = 1.5 \times 10^{-7} \text{ N}$$

Force due to reflection (change in momentum is twice that of absorption):
$$P_{\text{ref}} = 0.5 \times 90 = 45 \text{ W}$$
$$F_{\text{ref}} = \frac{2 P_{\text{ref}}}{c} = \frac{2 \times 45}{3 \times 10^8} = \frac{90}{3 \times 10^8} = 3 \times 10^{-7} \text{ N}$$

Total force:
$$F_{\text{total}} = F_{\text{abs}} + F_{\text{ref}} = (1.5 + 3) \times 10^{-7} = 4.5 \times 10^{-7} \text{ N}$$

Thus the correct option is A: $4.5 \times 10^{-7}$ N.
